x_sleepappetite_lin.how: PubMed record read through the NCBI E-utilities API

x_sleepappetite_fenton.publisher: Journal of Human Nutrition and Dietetics, 2021

x_sleepappetite_tasali.title: Effect of sleep extension on objectively assessed energy intake among adults with overweight in real-life settings: a randomized clinical trial

x_sleepappetite_depner.says: Groups of 8 to 14 young adults. Weekend recovery sleep did not prevent higher after-dinner intake and weight gain once short nights resumed; insulin sensitivity fell 9 to 27%.

x_sleepappetite_sletten.title: The importance of sleep regularity: a consensus statement of the National Sleep Foundation sleep timing and variability panel

x_sleepappetite_roenneberg.title: Social jetlag and obesity

x_sleepappetite_chang.title: Evening use of light-emitting eReaders negatively affects sleep, circadian timing, and next-morning alertness
x_sleepappetite_chang.publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2015
x_sleepappetite_chang.how: PubMed record read through the NCBI E-utilities API
x_sleepappetite_chang.says: Reading a light-emitting eBook before bed, against a printed book, delayed sleep onset, reduced evening sleepiness and melatonin, delayed the circadian clock and reduced next-morning alertness.

x_sleepappetite_hartstein.title: The impact of screen use on sleep health across the lifespan: a National Sleep Foundation consensus statement
x_sleepappetite_hartstein.how: PubMed record read through the NCBI E-utilities API
x_sleepappetite_hartstein.says: 16-person panel reached consensus on 5 of 10 statements: screen use impairs sleep in children and adolescents, and behavioural strategies may attenuate screen effects on sleep.

x_sleepappetite_vujovic.says: Randomised crossover trial controlling nutrient intake, activity, sleep and light. Late eating increased hunger and the 24-hour ghrelin to leptin ratio, and decreased waketime energy expenditure.

x_sleepappetite_young.title: Distribution of energy intake across the day and weight loss: a systematic review and meta-analysis
x_sleepappetite_young.how: PubMed record read through the NCBI E-utilities API
x_sleepappetite_young.says: 9 randomised trials. Within an energy-reduced diet, earlier distribution of intake gave 1.23 kg greater weight loss; described as short-term.

x_sleepappetite_garaulet.title: Timing of food intake predicts weight loss effectiveness
x_sleepappetite_garaulet.how: PubMed record read through the NCBI E-utilities API
x_sleepappetite_garaulet.says: 420 people in a 20-week programme in Spain. Those eating the main meal after 3 pm lost less weight, although energy intake, diet composition, estimated expenditure, appetite hormones and sleep duration were similar.

x_sleepappetite_kinsey.title: The health impact of nighttime eating: old and new perspectives

x_sleepappetite_gardineralc.title: The effect of alcohol on subsequent sleep in healthy adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis
x_sleepappetite_gardineralc.how: PubMed record read through the NCBI E-utilities API
x_sleepappetite_gardineralc.says: 27 studies. REM sleep was disrupted from a low dose (about two standard drinks) and worsened with dose; shorter sleep onset was seen only at a high dose (about five standard drinks).

x_sleepappetite_ebrahim.title: Alcohol and sleep I: effects on normal sleep
x_sleepappetite_ebrahim.how: PubMed record read through the NCBI E-utilities API

x_sleepappetite_jpsleep.title: Sleep Guide for Health Promotion 2023

x_sleepappetite_hill.title: Stress and eating behaviours in healthy adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis
x_sleepappetite_hill.how: PubMed record read through the NCBI E-utilities API
x_sleepappetite_hill.says: 54 studies, 119,820 people. Stress had a small positive association with overall intake (g = 0.114), more unhealthy food (g = 0.116) and less healthy food (g = -0.111).

x_sleepappetite_nhsinsomnia.title: Insomnia
x_sleepappetite_nhsinsomnia.says: Lists stress, anxiety or depression first among the most common causes of insomnia. Self-help includes going to bed only when sleepy, getting up at the same time every day and not sleeping in after a bad night.

x_sleepappetite_robinson.title: Eating attentively: a systematic review and meta-analysis of the effect of food intake memory and awareness on eating

x_sleepappetite_robinson.says: 24 studies. Distracted eating raised immediate intake (SMD 0.39) and later intake more (SMD 0.76); removing visual information about the amount eaten raised immediate intake (SMD 0.48).

x_sleepappetite_hollandsprox.title: Altering the availability or proximity of food, alcohol, and tobacco products to change their selection and consumption
x_sleepappetite_hollandsprox.how: PubMed record read through the NCBI E-utilities API
x_sleepappetite_hollandsprox.says: Food placed farther away was eaten moderately less (SMD -0.60, 12 studies, 1,098 people, low certainty); the effect was greater the farther away it was placed. Most studies were in laboratories.

x_sleepappetite_niddkdef.title: Definition and facts for binge eating disorder
x_sleepappetite_niddkdef.publisher: US National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases, 2021
x_sleepappetite_niddkdef.says: Binge eating is a large amount of food in a short time with a feeling of lost control; regular binges at least once a week for 3 months may mean binge eating disorder. It is the most common eating disorder in the US; many more people have binge episodes too infrequent to meet the criteria.

x_sleepappetite_niddksym.title: Symptoms and causes of binge eating disorder
x_sleepappetite_niddksym.publisher: US National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases, 2021
x_sleepappetite_niddksym.says: Based on DSM-5: a large amount of food in a short time, for example within 2 hours, with lack of control; may also eat quickly, until uncomfortably full, when not hungry, alone from embarrassment, and feel disgusted, depressed or guilty afterwards.

x_sleepappetite_udo.says: 36,306 US adults. Binge eating disorder: lifetime 0.85%, 12-month 0.44%; odds significantly greater for women than men.

x_sleepappetite_nimhstats.title: Eating disorders (statistics)
x_sleepappetite_nimhstats.publisher: US National Institute of Mental Health
x_sleepappetite_nimhstats.says: From the 2001 to 2003 National Comorbidity Survey Replication: past-year binge eating disorder 1.2% of adults (1.6% of women, 0.8% of men); lifetime 2.8%.

x_sleepappetite_nhsbed.title: Overview: binge eating disorder
x_sleepappetite_nhsbed.says: If you think you may have binge eating disorder, see a GP as soon as you can. Most people recover with the right support and treatment; the main treatments are guided self-help and cognitive behavioural therapy.

x_sleepappetite_hilbert.title: Meta-analysis of the efficacy of psychological and medical treatments for binge-eating disorder
x_sleepappetite_hilbert.publisher: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology, 2019
x_sleepappetite_hilbert.how: PubMed record read through the NCBI E-utilities API
x_sleepappetite_hilbert.says: 81 trials, 7,515 people. Psychotherapy, mostly cognitive behavioural therapy, showed large effects on binge episodes against inactive controls; overall evidence quality was very low.

x_sleepappetite_qaseem.title: Management of chronic insomnia disorder in adults: a clinical practice guideline from the American College of Physicians
x_sleepappetite_qaseem.how: PubMed record read through the NCBI E-utilities API
x_sleepappetite_qaseem.says: Recommends that all adults receive cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia as the initial treatment for chronic insomnia disorder (strong recommendation, moderate-quality evidence).

x_sleepappetite_riemann.title: The European Insomnia Guideline: an update on the diagnosis and treatment of insomnia 2023
x_sleepappetite_riemann.how: PubMed record read through the NCBI E-utilities API
x_sleepappetite_riemann.says: Cognitive-behavioural therapy for insomnia is recommended as first-line treatment for chronic insomnia in adults of any age, in person or digitally (grade A).

x_sleepappetite_trauer.how: PubMed record read through the NCBI E-utilities API
x_sleepappetite_trauer.says: 20 trials, 1,162 people. Sleep onset improved by 19.03 minutes and wake after sleep onset by 26.00 minutes; programmes combined at least 3 of cognitive therapy, stimulus control, sleep restriction, sleep hygiene and relaxation.

x_sleepappetite_edinger.how: PubMed record read through the NCBI E-utilities API
x_sleepappetite_edinger.says: Strong recommendation for multicomponent CBT for insomnia; conditional for stimulus control, sleep restriction and relaxation alone; conditional recommendation against sleep hygiene as a single-component therapy.

x_sleepappetite_chung.how: PubMed record read through the NCBI E-utilities API
x_sleepappetite_chung.says: 15 studies. Sleep hygiene education gave small to medium improvements but was significantly less efficacious than CBT for insomnia.

x_sleepappetite_irish.title: The role of sleep hygiene in promoting public health: a review of empirical evidence
x_sleepappetite_irish.how: PubMed record read through the NCBI E-utilities API
x_sleepappetite_irish.says: Review. Individual sleep hygiene recommendations are associated with sleep, but their direct effects remain largely untested in the general population.

x_sleepappetite_stutz.how: PubMed record read through the NCBI E-utilities API

x_sleepappetite_kredlow.how: PubMed record read through the NCBI E-utilities API

sections.heading: How a short night changes hunger

paragraphs.text: Short sleep raises hunger and food intake fairly consistently, while hormone changes are less consistent. Across 41 randomised trials, restricted sleep raised hunger ratings and led people to eat about 253 more calories a day. The review found no strong evidence that average levels of the appetite hormones leptin or ghrelin changed.

support.quote: We identified 41 randomized controlled trials using sleep restriction intervention.

Sleep restriction resulted in a significant increase in subjective hunger on a 100 mm scale (mean difference = 13.4, p < 0.001). Participants consumed 252.8 more kcal/d (p = 0.011) under sleep restriction than under normal sleep.
we did not find strong evidence supporting the significant impact of sleep restriction on mean leptin or ghrelin levels or energy expenditure

paragraphs.text: Other pooled studies point the same way, with a small rise in ghrelin, a hormone that drives hunger. A review of 21 studies with 2,250 people found slightly higher ghrelin in short sleepers. Another analysis found that sleeping 5.5 hours or less raised daily intake by about 204 calories.

support.quote: Twenty-one of 3536 studies, covering a total of 2250 participants, met the inclusion criteria.
Ghrelin levels were higher in the short sleep group (standard mean difference [SMD] = 0.14
Partial sleep restriction with duration of ≤5.5 h day-1 increases daily energy intake
with a mean difference of 204 kcal (95% CI = 112-295; P < 0.001) in daily energy intake

paragraphs.text: Short sleep may also change which foods appeal. In a study of 12 young men, two short nights raised hunger by 24% and appetite for calorie-dense, high-carbohydrate foods by 33 to 45%. In a brain-imaging study, sleep loss dulled frontal areas that weigh food choices and raised desire for high-calorie foods.

support.quote: 12 healthy men
2 days of sleep restriction and 2 days of sleep extension
increased hunger (increase, 24%; P < 0.01) and appetite (increase, 23%; P = 0.01), especially for calorie-dense foods with high carbohydrate content (increase, 33% to 45%; P = 0.02)
sleep deprivation significantly decreases activity in appetitive evaluation regions within the human frontal cortex and insular cortex during food desirability choices
a significant increase in the desire for weight-gain promoting high-calorie foods following sleep deprivation

sections.heading: Why the extra eating comes late

paragraphs.text: After short nights, much of the extra food tends to be eaten after dinner. In an inpatient study of 16 adults, five short nights raised energy burned by about 5%, but intake rose by more, especially at night after dinner. Weight rose about 0.8 kg, and the women showed less dietary restraint.

support.quote: We studied 16 adults in a 14- to 15-d-long inpatient study

insufficient sleep increased total daily energy expenditure by ∼5%; however, energy intake--especially at night after dinner--was in excess of energy needed to maintain energy balance. Insufficient sleep led to 0.82 ± 0.47 kg (±SD) weight gain
insufficient sleep reduced dietary restraint and led to weight gain in women

paragraphs.text: Sleeping longer reduced intake in a trial of people who usually slept too little. Among 80 adults with overweight who slept under 6.5 hours a night, one counselling session added about 1.2 hours of sleep. That group then ate about 270 fewer calories a day than the control group.

support.quote: had habitual sleep duration of less than 6.5 hours per night
an individualized sleep hygiene counseling session that was intended to extend their bedtime to 8.5 hours
Data from 80 randomized participants
Sleep duration was increased by approximately 1.2 hours per night
The sleep extension group had a significant decrease in energy intake compared with the control group (-270 kcal/d

paragraphs.text: Going to bed and getting up at consistent times may matter as much as total sleep. In 60,977 UK adults tracked by wrist devices, the more regular sleepers had a 20 to 48% lower risk of death. Regularity predicted risk better than sleep length. The study was observational.

support.quote: from > 10 million hours of accelerometer data in 60 977 UK Biobank participants
Higher sleep regularity was associated with a 20%-48% lower risk of all-cause mortality
Sleep regularity was a stronger predictor of all-cause mortality than sleep duration

paragraphs.text: A US expert panel agreed that regular sleep timing is important for health, safety and performance. The panel, convened by the National Sleep Foundation, reviewed 63 publications. It judged weekend catch-up sleep may help when weekday sleep is short, but in one small trial, lie-ins did not stop extra eating after dinner.

support.quote: The literature search and panel review identified 63 full text publications to inform consensus voting.

Consistency of sleep onset and offset timing is important for health, safety, and performance. Nonetheless, when insufficient sleep is obtained during the week/work days, weekend/non-work day catch-up sleep may be beneficial.
during recurrent insufficient sleep following the weekend, the circadian phase was delayed, and after-dinner energy intake and body weight increased versus baseline
control (CON; 9-h sleep opportunities, n = 8)

paragraphs.text: A gap between the body clock and the hours that work demands is linked to higher body weight. In a large population study, this social jetlag was linked to a higher body mass index, beyond the effect of sleep length. It shows a link, not a cause.

support.quote: Social jetlag quantifies the discrepancy that often arises between circadian and social clocks
we report the results from a large-scale epidemiological study, showing that, beyond sleep duration, social jetlag is associated with increased BMI

paragraphs.text: A bright screen in the evening can push the body clock later. In a controlled study, reading on a light-emitting e-reader before bed instead of a printed book meant taking longer to fall asleep, less melatonin, a later body clock and lower alertness the next morning.

support.quote: Participants reading an LE-eBook took longer to fall asleep and had reduced evening sleepiness, reduced melatonin secretion, later timing of their circadian clock, and reduced next-morning alertness than when reading a printed book.

paragraphs.text: Experts agree more firmly about screens and sleep in young people than in adults. A National Sleep Foundation panel of 16 experts agreed that screen use impairs sleep in children and adolescents. It agreed on only 5 of 10 statements, and judged that changing screen habits may reduce the harm.

support.quote: The National Sleep Foundation convened a 16-person multidisciplinary expert panel
ultimately achieving consensus on 5 out of the 10 statements
(1) in general, screen use impairs sleep health among children and adolescents
(3) behavioral strategies and interventions may attenuate the negative effects of screen use on sleep health

paragraphs.text: Blue-light-filtering glasses have not been shown to improve sleep. A Cochrane review of 17 small trials found mixed results for sleep quality and rated the evidence very low in certainty. The data were too uneven to pool, and the authors called for better trials.

support.quote: We included 17 RCTs, with sample sizes ranging from five to 156 participants
We do not know if blue-light filtering spectacle lenses are equivalent or superior to non-blue-light filtering spectacle lenses with respect to sleep quality (very low-certainty evidence).
We did not perform meta-analyses for any of the outcome measures
Future high-quality randomised trials are required

paragraphs.text: Eating the same food later in the day raised hunger in a tightly controlled trial. Adults with overweight ate identical meals on early and late schedules. The late schedule increased hunger, raised the ratio of ghrelin to the fullness hormone leptin, and lowered energy burned while awake.

support.quote: we conducted a randomized, controlled, crossover trial (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02298790) to determine the effects of late versus early eating while rigorously controlling for nutrient intake, physical activity, sleep, and light exposure
Late eating increased hunger
increasing waketime and 24-h ghrelin:leptin ratio
late eating decreased waketime energy expenditure

paragraphs.text: Eating more of the day's food earlier helped weight loss a little in short trials. A pooled analysis of 9 randomised trials found that, within a reduced-calorie diet, an earlier pattern led to about 1.2 kg more weight loss. The authors describe this as short-term and call for more studies.

support.quote: nine randomized controlled trials investigating the impact of energy intake distribution on weight loss were identified
in the context of an energy-reduced diet, distributing energy intake with a focus on earlier intake resulted in significantly greater weight loss (-1.23 kg
a focus on earlier intakes can result in greater short-term weight loss compared with later intakes. Future studies are needed

paragraphs.text: The research does not show that any food after a set hour is harmful. In a Spanish observational study of 420 dieters, late main-meal eaters lost less weight despite similar intake. A review found harm mainly with large meals in people eating most of their food at night, while snacks of about 150 calories did not appear harmful.

support.quote: a sample of 420 individuals who followed a 20-week weight-loss treatment

Late lunch eaters lost less weight and displayed a slower weight-loss rate during the 20 weeks of treatment than early eaters (P=0.002). Surprisingly, energy intake, dietary composition, estimated energy expenditure, appetite hormones and sleep duration was similar between both groups.
negative outcomes have been demonstrated in response to large mixed meals in populations that consume a majority of their daily food intake during the night
nighttime consumption of small (~150 kcals) single nutrients or mixed-meals does not appear to be harmful

paragraphs.text: Even two drinks in the evening can disturb dream sleep. A pooled analysis of 27 studies found that about two standard drinks reduced REM sleep, the dreaming stage, and more alcohol made it worse. Falling asleep faster was seen only after about five drinks.

support.quote: A systematic search of the literature identified 27 studies for inclusion in the analysis.
disruptions to REM sleep occurred following consumption of a low dose of alcohol (≤0.50 g∙kg-1 or approximately two standard drinks) and progressively worsened with increasing doses of alcohol

Reductions in sleep onset latency and latency to deep sleep (i.e., non-rapid eye movement stage three (N3)) were only observed following the consumption of a high dose of alcohol (≥0.85∙g kg-1 or approximately five standard drinks).

paragraphs.text: Alcohol can help people drop off, but sleep later in the night suffers. A review of studies in healthy volunteers found more broken sleep in the second half of the night at all doses. Japan's sleep guide advises against heavy drinking and nightcaps, and suggests seeing a doctor if sleep seems to need one.

support.quote: At all dosages, alcohol causes a reduction in sleep onset latency, a more consolidated first half sleep and an increase in sleep disruption in the second half of sleep.
consuming large amounts of alcohol (heavy drinking) or daily drinking, including the so-called "nightcap," are not recommended for good sleep
Consultation with a physician is recommended if you have insomnia symptoms that may lead to the need for nightcaps.

paragraphs.text: Stress tends to tilt eating toward less healthy food, though the effect is small. Across 54 studies with nearly 120,000 adults, a pooled analysis linked stress to slightly more eating overall, more unhealthy food and less healthy food. Stress also tops the NHS list of common causes of insomnia, alongside anxiety and depression.

support.quote: 54 studies (combined N = 119,820) were retained in the meta-analysis. A small, positive effect size was found for the stress-overall food intake relationship (Hedges' g = 0.114). Stress was associated with increased consumption of unhealthy foods (Hedges' g = 0.116) but decreased consumption of healthy foods (Hedges' g = -0.111).
The most common causes of insomnia are: stress, anxiety or depression

paragraphs.text: Eating while distracted, for example at a screen, raises intake at that meal and later. Across 24 studies, distraction moderately increased how much was eaten at the time, and later intake even more. Not being able to see how much had been eaten also raised intake.

support.quote: Twenty-four studies were reviewed. Evidence indicated that eating when distracted produced a moderate increase in immediate intake (SMD: 0.39; 95% CI: 0.25, 0.53) but increased later intake to a greater extent (SMD: 0.76; 95% CI: 0.45, 1.07).
Removing visual information about the amount of food eaten during a meal increased immediate intake (SMD: 0.48; 95% CI: 0.27, 0.68).

paragraphs.text: Snacks placed farther away get eaten less. A Cochrane review found such food was eaten moderately less, across 12 studies with 1,098 people, and the effect grew with distance. Certainty was low, and most studies were laboratory tests. Keeping snacks in the kitchen, not on the desk, applies this idea.

support.quote: For consumption outcomes, meta-analysis of 15 comparisons from 12 studies (n = 1098) found that exposure to food placed farther away resulted in a moderate reduction in its consumption: SMD -0.60 (95% CI -0.84 to -0.36) (low certainty evidence).
this effect was greater: the farther away the product was placed
The majority were conducted in laboratory settings (14/24)

paragraphs.text: Binge eating disorder is a specific condition, different from sometimes eating more than planned. A US health institute describes a binge as a large amount of food in a short time, for example within 2 hours, with a feeling of lost control. Binges at least once a week for 3 months may point to the disorder.

support.quote: Binge eating is when you eat a large amount of food in a short amount of time and feel you can’t control what or how much you are eating. If you binge eat regularly—at least once a week for 3 months—you may have binge eating disorder.
eat a large amount of food in a short amount of time; for example, within 2 hours

paragraphs.text: Binge eating disorder also tends to involve eating very fast, past fullness and alone. Other signs are eating large amounts when not hungry, hiding it from embarrassment, and feeling disgusted, depressed or guilty afterwards. Unlike in bulimia, binges are not regularly followed by vomiting, laxatives, fasting or hard exercise.

support.quote: eat more quickly than usual during binge episodes eat until you feel uncomfortably full eat large amounts of food even when you are not hungry eat alone because you are embarrassed about the amount of food you eat feel disgusted, depressed, or guilty after overeating
People who have bulimia nervosa routinely try to prevent weight gain after binge eating by vomiting, using laxatives or diuretics , fasting, or exercising excessively.
but it is not a regular part of their binge-eating behavior

paragraphs.text: Binge eating disorder is uncommon, although it is the most common eating disorder in the US. A survey of 36,306 US adults found it in 0.44% over the past year and 0.85% at some point in life, more often in women. Binges too infrequent to meet the criteria are much more common.

support.quote: Binge eating disorder is the most common eating disorder in the United States
A national sample of 36,306 U.S. adults completed structured diagnostic interviews

Prevalence estimates of lifetime AN, BN, and BED were 0.80% (SE 0.07%), 0.28% (SE 0.03%), and 0.85% (SE 0.05%), respectively. Twelve-month estimates for AN, BN, and BED were 0.05% (SE 0.02%), 0.14% (SE 0.02%), and 0.44% (SE 0.04%).
The odds of lifetime and 12-month diagnoses of all three eating disorders were significantly greater for women than for men
A much larger percentage of teens and adults have episodes of binge eating or loss-of-control eating
Prevalence of binge eating disorder was twice as high among females (1.6%) than males (0.8%).

paragraphs.text: Anyone who thinks they may have binge eating disorder should see a GP soon, and effective treatment exists. The NHS reports that recovery is common with the right support, mainly guided self-help or cognitive behavioural therapy. Across 81 trials, psychotherapy, mostly of this kind, had large effects on binge episodes.

support.quote: If you think you may have binge eating disorder, see a GP as soon as you can.

paragraphs.text: For long-term insomnia, US and European guidelines recommend cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia as the first treatment. It combines parts such as stimulus control, sleep restriction, relaxation and work on thoughts about sleep. Across 20 trials, it helped people fall asleep about 19 minutes faster and spend 26 fewer minutes awake.

The American Academy of Sleep Medicine advises against using sleep hygiene as a stand-alone therapy for insomnia, and 15 pooled studies found it less effective than cognitive behavioural therapy. paragraphs.text: The popular advice to avoid all evening exercise is not supported by pooled studies. Across 23 studies, evening exercise did not harm sleep, though vigorous exercise ending within an hour of bedtime might. In a separate analysis of 66 studies, regular exercise had small to moderate benefits for sleep.
